summary: Clarifies how Globally Routable User Agent URIs (GRUUs) should be used with the SIP event notification framework. Experience after RFC 6665 showed that the original text left room for different readings. This document spells out the intended behavior and updates RFC 6665.

plainLanguage.summary: Two people kept reading the same rule differently, so someone wrote a short note saying what the rule really meant, like a teacher clarifying a confusing homework question.

questions: what is a gruu in sip
how do gruus work with sip event notifications
does a sip notifier have to use a gruu
subtitle: A short fix that spells out when a SIP notifier must use a GRUU as its local target.

tldr.problem: RFC 6665 said notifiers MUST use a GRUU as their local target, but implementors read that in different ways, including whether it covered dialogs created by INVITE.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 7621 replaces the text: notifiers MUST use a GRUU for all dialog-forming and target-refresh methods, except dialogs where they will reject all subscription requests.
tldr.outcome: The requirement is explicit, INVITE dialogs are included, and a notifier using a non-GRUU contact must reject subscription attempts, normally with 403 (Forbidden).

today: RFC 7621 is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 6665. No later RFC is recorded as obsoleting or updating it.

sections.title: Why a Clarification Was Needed
sections.content:
RFC 7621 exists to fix a point of implementor confusion caused by unclear wording in RFC 6665, the SIP event notification framework. It updates that RFC and adds no new protocol machinery.

The disputed text is in Section 4.5.1 of RFC 6665: notifiers MUST implement the Globally Routable User Agent URI (GRUU) extension from RFC 5627, and MUST use a GRUU as their local target.
sections.plainLanguage: A rule in a big rulebook was worded loosely, so people played the game differently. This note says what the rule meant.

sections.title: What the Original Rule Meant
sections.content:
The point of the GRUU requirement is to let a subscriber send SUBSCRIBE or REFER requests to one specific user agent, where the subscription target might be something like an INVITE dialog on that device.

So the requirement was meant to cover the local target of all dialogs, including those created by INVITE, not only dialogs created by SUBSCRIBE. Implementors interpreted it in a variety of ways.
sections.plainLanguage: A GRUU is like a direct phone extension for one device, so a caller reaches that exact device and not just the whole household.

sections.title: The Replacement Text
sections.content:
Notifiers MUST implement GRUU and MUST use a GRUU as their local target for all dialog-forming methods and all target-refresh methods. The exception is for dialogs where the notifier will reject all subscription requests, implicit or explicit. The RFC notes that using a GRUU there causes no harm either. The requirement specifically includes dialogs created by INVITE.

A notifier that uses a non-GRUU local contact under the exception MUST reject any request that might create a subscription to that dialog, whether it comes from SUBSCRIBE or REFER. The rejection code SHOULD be 403 (Forbidden) unless another code fits better.
sections.plainLanguage: Use the direct extension everywhere, unless you promise never to take subscriptions on that call. If you make that promise, you must say no when someone tries.

sections.title: Security and IANA
sections.content: The mechanism does not introduce any security issues beyond those discussed in RFC 6665. The document requests no actions of IANA.
sections.plainLanguage: The note makes nothing riskier than before, and nobody needs to update any lists.
